title: Nawab Kapoor Singh, the Nihang Chief

blocks.text: Dohra:

(Dear readers) listen to the episode of first Nawabhip, Which was conferred on a Singh named S. Kapoor Singh. He had earned this title from the Mughals, By dint of the great deeds of warriorship done by him. (1)
lines: (Dear readers) listen to the episode of first Nawabhip,
Which was conferred on a Singh named S.
Kapoor Singh.
He had earned this title from the Mughals,
By dint of the great deeds of warriorship done by him.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Now I (the author) would narrate the episode of S. Kapoor Singh, As my ancestors have narrated it to me. When Banda Singh Bahadur conquered all the Mughals, He turned hostile to the (mainstream) Khalsa Panth. (2)
lines: Now I (the author) would narrate the episode of S.
Kapoor Singh,
As my ancestors have narrated it to me.
When Banda Singh Bahadur conquered all the Mughals,
He turned hostile to the (mainstream) Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: As the moment of his destined doom approached near, He intended to get the (mainstream) Khalsa Panth eliminated. Seeing through Baba Banda Singh's game plan, The Khalsa Panth forces departed and settled at Guru Chak2 . (3)
lines: As the moment of his destined doom approached near,
He intended to get the (mainstream) Khalsa Panth eliminated.
Seeing through Baba Banda Singh's game plan,
The Khalsa Panth forces departed and settled at Guru Chak2 .

blocks.text: As the Mughals heard about the division in the Khalsa ranks, They felt delighted at the birth of such a development. As they were always keen to cause a rift between the Khalsa ranks, They sent their representatives with a financial package to the Singhs. (4)
lines: As the Mughals heard about the division in the Khalsa ranks,
They felt delighted at the birth of such a development.
As they were always keen to cause a rift between the Khalsa ranks,
They sent their representatives with a financial package to the Singhs.

blocks.text: Adopting a posture of flattering and pampering the Singhs, They feigned to be always at the beck and call of the Singhs.
Swearing an oath on the holy Koran3 time and again, They swore never to set foot on the soil of Guru Chak. (5)
lines: Swearing an oath on the holy Koran3 time and again,
They swore never to set foot on the soil of Guru Chak.

blocks.text: Asking the Singhs to hold congregation without any fear, The Singhs could assemble at Nankana Sahib4 and Rori Sahib5 . They could congregate at the holy shrines of Dera Baba Nanak6 and Khandoor Sahib7 , As well as at Taran Taran and other holy Sikh shrines. (6)
lines: Asking the Singhs to hold congregation without any fear,
The Singhs could assemble at Nankana Sahib4 and Rori Sahib5 .
They could congregate at the holy shrines of Dera Baba Nanak6 and Khandoor Sahib7 ,
As well as at Taran Taran and other holy Sikh shrines.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Exhorting the Singhs to hold congregations fearlessly, At all those places which had been the abodes of the Gurus. The Mughals would not only exempt these congregations from taxation, But they themselves would provide security to these gatherings. (7)
lines: Exhorting the Singhs to hold congregations fearlessly,
At all those places which had been the abodes of the Gurus.
The Mughals would not only exempt these congregations from taxation,
But they themselves would provide security to these gatherings.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

In this way they won the confidence of the Khalsa Panth, By holding out several kinds of promises and assurances. Holding out promises of providing employment, They invited the needy among the Sikhs to approach them. (8)
lines: In this way they won the confidence of the Khalsa Panth,
By holding out several kinds of promises and assurances.
Holding out promises of providing employment,
They invited the needy among the Sikhs to approach them.

blocks.text: Approaching the veterans Baba Binod Singh and Kahan Singh, They won their allegiance by presenting moneybags, Allowing them to keep a contingent of five hundred Singhs each, They won the support of many other Singhs with their help. (9)
lines: Approaching the veterans Baba Binod Singh and Kahan Singh,
They won their allegiance by presenting moneybags,
Allowing them to keep a contingent of five hundred Singhs each,
They won the support of many other Singhs with their help.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Adopting such tactics and (dangling out such temptations), The Mughals managed to win over the Khalsa Singhs. But still they were as much scared of Banda Singh, As a (timid) quail feels scared of a (ferocious) hawk. (10)
lines: Adopting such tactics and (dangling out such temptations),
The Mughals managed to win over the Khalsa Singhs.
But still they were as much scared of Banda Singh,
As a (timid) quail feels scared of a (ferocious) hawk.

blocks.text: Even as the Mughals were marking time (for the right opportunity), The Khalsa Panth, too, was looking for the opportune moment, Both sides being equal claimants of being sovereigns, Both nursed ambitions of waging a war against each other. (11)
lines: Even as the Mughals were marking time (for the right opportunity),
The Khalsa Panth, too, was looking for the opportune moment,
Both sides being equal claimants of being sovereigns,
Both nursed ambitions of waging a war against each other.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Mughals kept on offering financial doles, The Singhs kept on receiving these doles at Guru Chak daily. S. Darbara Singh8 who had been the Diwan9 of the Khalsa Panth, Had also been the treasurer of Khalsa Panth's finances. (12)
lines: As the Mughals kept on offering financial doles,
The Singhs kept on receiving these doles at Guru Chak daily.
S.
Darbara Singh8 who had been the Diwan9 of the Khalsa Panth,
Had also been the treasurer of Khalsa Panth's finances.

blocks.text: Since he was highly venerated among the Khalsa Panth, He used to keep all the factions in good humour. Since no body considered him as his rival, He used to disburse uniforms to every one. (13)
lines: Since he was highly venerated among the Khalsa Panth,
He used to keep all the factions in good humour.
Since no body considered him as his rival,
He used to disburse uniforms to every one.

blocks.text: He ran a single community kitchen for the entire Khalsa force, As well as issued dresses and clothing to everyone. The Khalsa Panth went on flourishing in this way, Even as they kept on indulging in factional fights as well. (14)
lines: He ran a single community kitchen for the entire Khalsa force,
As well as issued dresses and clothing to everyone.
The Khalsa Panth went on flourishing in this way,
Even as they kept on indulging in factional fights as well.

blocks.text: [They (the Mughals) wished to eliminate the Singhs]
Dohra:

No sooner did the Mughals manage to capture Banda Singh, Than they changed their stance (towards the Singhs). They, now, were too keen to eliminate the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs, Along with all others (Bandhayees) in one single stroke. (1)
lines: No sooner did the Mughals manage to capture Banda Singh,
Than they changed their stance (towards the Singhs).
They, now, were too keen to eliminate the (Tat Khalsa) Singhs,
Along with all others (Bandhayees) in one single stroke.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The (Tat Khalsa) Singhs, far from falling into their trap, Moved their camp farther from Guru Chak (into countryside). As the Singhs kept shifting their positions and locations, The Mughals also got obsessed with chasing the Singhs. (2)
lines: The (Tat Khalsa) Singhs, far from falling into their trap,
Moved their camp farther from Guru Chak (into countryside).
As the Singhs kept shifting their positions and locations,
The Mughals also got obsessed with chasing the Singhs.

blocks.text: The Singhs possessed neither any fort nor sanctuary, Where they could take cover and fight back. Neither did Singhs had possession of any mountains, From where they could fight the Mughals from a vantage-point. (3)
lines: The Singhs possessed neither any fort nor sanctuary,
Where they could take cover and fight back.
Neither did Singhs had possession of any mountains,
From where they could fight the Mughals from a vantage-point.

blocks.text: At many places, Singhs had a straight fight with the Mughals, But sacrificed their lives when pressed too much. The Khalsa Panth landed itself in such a helpless situation, That they had to seek shelter in the wilds and ravines. (4)
lines: At many places,
Singhs had a straight fight with the Mughals,
But sacrificed their lives when pressed too much.
The Khalsa Panth landed itself in such a helpless situation,
That they had to seek shelter in the wilds and ravines.

blocks.text: Sortha:

Banda Singh had let out a curse on the Khalsa Panth, When he had to confine himself in the fort (at Gurdas Nangal). The Khalsa Panth had to bear the consequences of their sinful act, Of not reaching out to the support of Banda Singh. (5)
lines: Banda Singh had let out a curse on the Khalsa Panth,
When he had to confine himself in the fort (at Gurdas Nangal).
The Khalsa Panth had to bear the consequences of their sinful act,
Of not reaching out to the support of Banda Singh.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Thereafter the Singhs scattered themselves helter-skelter, In the bands of small and big numbers. They started marking time somehow or the other, Either in each other's vicinity or at a distance. (6)
lines: Thereafter the Singhs scattered themselves helter-skelter,
In the bands of small and big numbers.
They started marking time somehow or the other,
Either in each other's vicinity or at a distance.

blocks.text: In between this episode of Singh's (helpless ordeal), Let me narrate another episode as well. After that I would narrate the episode of Nawabship, As it came to be conferred on S. Kapoor Singh. (7)
lines: In between this episode of Singh's (helpless ordeal),
Let me narrate another episode as well.
After that I would narrate the episode of Nawabship,
As it came to be conferred on S.
Kapoor Singh.
